methods.input_time: frontend handler receipt, not hardware input
methods.state_matching: semantic render/peek/scroll followed by callback with required state or content geometry
methods.wheel_intervals: active scroll callback segments including each terminal callback; idle gaps excluded
methods.resize_intervals: callbacks from first receipt through final matching callback of each observed resize burst
methods.monitor_exclusion: all selected phase and burst monitor eligibility flags must be true

excluded.portrait: Moved off its target monitor; user chose to finish primary only.

restoration.pointer_difference_scope: desktop session guard, excluded from frontend timing

limits: Manual gesture trajectories, event counts, resize ranges, and phase durations differ.
Callback cadence does not prove physical presentation FPS.
Resize receipt endpoints differ and intermediate updates can be coalesced.
Wheel response can include motion from an earlier spring input.
CPU/PSS excludes GPU and compositor cost; fixture backend cost excludes real store scanning.
Short monitor crossings between geometry samples cannot be ruled out.
No overall speedup or CPU ranking is established.
recommendation: Keep Python in production. This evidence does not justify a full migration; Qt resize callback tails were lower in one run, wheel cadence was unchanged, and observed PSS was higher.
